This pro, however, is somewhat canceled out by lack of removable storage. If I could swap out batteries and memory cards I wouldn't be tied to my laptop so much. I would like the ability to record in non-hd to maximize storage but if that's an option I can't find it.

And while the large lens looks great, the fact that it protrudes so much makes it a fingerprint magnet.

The included Flip-share software is pretty cool, I wish it had the capability to view and share video from other devices.

text_fidelity_a:
TP-Link Wireless N300 PCI Adapter, 2.4GHz 300Mbps -(TL-WN851ND) While there isn't as great a NEED for this as there used to be, as so many devices have built in wireless, when you have a tower that needs it, this is the answer.
Basically, because of even the higher demands (Skype, streaming, etc) you need that strong signal without drops, both ways. This has a feature called MIMO, which instead of the standard adapter that has one antenna for reception, THIS has multiple antennae to accommodate 2 ways, and to reduce drops in data.
Be sure you disable the anti-virus, failure to do so and it just doesn't work. If you periodically lose the signal and require a reboot, then uninstall the driver in utility, and install the driver only. Then use Windows embedded wireless utility to connect to your wireless network.

Go to the manufacturer site for some excellent recommendations, like if there's a reduction in signal after a few months, set the router to a static channel (like 1, 3, 6, or 9).
For the money, this seems to be a pretty good product, at least in my case.
I've had very good experiences this company's products, as well as customer service.
text_fidelity_b: TP-Link Wireless N300 PCI Adapter, 2.4GHz 300Mbps -(TL-WN851ND)

text_fidelity_a:
Fire 7 Tablet (7" display, 16 GB) - Yellow - (Previous Generation - 7th) This is not a replacement for an iPad or other high end tablet by any means, but it is very functional and fun. I had to use it as a phone for about a month, and here’s what I have to say

PROS
• excellent kindle app
- realistic page flip
- text to word function reads for you
- make notes and highlight in text
- get updates on how long it should take you to read.
- much more
• Acceses internet and has applications for weather and such
• can be used to map places and text provided you have WiFi
• can take pictures and videos
• lots of classic books can be found for free.

CONS
• Low Resolution Screen
• very low resolution camera and video
• unless jail broken, can only use Amazon apps, which significantly lowers what apps you can get
• over 20 preinstalled apps that cannot be removed and will never get used

Overall thoughts:
This device is a fraction of the cost of higher end tablets, and it therefore has a fraction of the functions. It is very affordable and will work fine for what you may need it for. I found that I liked it as a notebook with the Evernote app.
The comparable device would be the nook and it has google play so more apps, but their reader system has fewer free classic books.
text_fidelity_b: Fire 7 Tablet (7" display, 16 GB) - Yellow - (Previous Generation - 7th)

text_fidelity_a:
TOZO T6 True Wireless Earbuds Bluetooth 5.3 Headphones Touch Control with Wireless Charging Case IPX8 Waterproof Stereo Earphones in-Ear Built-in Mic Headset Premium Deep Bass White (2022 Upgraded) For the money and considering I've only used these ear buds for 1 day they are an exceptional buy. I work mostly outdoors (Florida) in grounds keeping with noisy equipment and lots of sweat. They charged quickly and paired without issue. The range from transmitting device is basic at best with them occasionally losing signal when phone is in pocket and I bend over and have my ear muffs on. I can get about 30' away from phone if there isn't any obstructions. They hold their charge well. They are pretty comfortable to wear especially since I typically have ear muffs over them. As for noise canceling I don't notice any difference than any other in ear bud but my ear muffs fit over these just fine.

My only complaint really is the sound quality. Mids and highs are decent for this price range but there isn't really any lows. They are small devices so I'm not looking to thump but I'm not impressed compared to others I've worn.

I will update as I get more time on them.
text_fidelity_b: TOZO T6 True Wireless Earbuds Bluetooth 5.3 Headphones Touch Control with Wireless Charging Case IPX8 Waterproof Stereo Earphones in-Ear Built-in Mic Headset Premium Deep Bass White (2022 Upgraded)

text_fidelity_a:
Kindle Oasis E-reader (Previous Generation - 9th) – Graphite, 7" High-Resolution Display (300 ppi), Waterproof, Built-In Audible, 32 GB, Wi-Fi - with Special Offers (Closeout) I purchased one of these 9th generation Kindle Oasis. The first unit I received would freeze during the configuration process. You could reset it, but if you try to configure, it would freeze again. At this point, I made the mistake of asking for a replacement instead of just returning the faulty Kindle Oasis for a refund. A replacement unit arrived in three days. Unfortunately, the replacement unit was DoA. There was a fixed image on screen, and I wasn't able to get a response from this Kindle after charging it for a long time and multiple reset attempts. I had already shipped the first unit back using a UPS shipping label created by Amazon at this point. I went to my Amazon Orders page to return the second unit for a credit. But Amazon web interface wouldn't allow a self service return for refund. I had contact customer service and deal with several customer service representatives. They consistently asked me to try some simple trouble shooting steps ( most of which are not even applicable if you have a completely dead kindle). They wouldn't listen to me when I said I just wanted to return it, and try to pressure me into another replacement. At this point, I had spent several hours troubleshooting, talking to Amazon Customer service, taking packages to UPS, etc. so I insisted on a return for refund. This time, the customer service representative said he was having problems generating the return label, and then disappeared. After several minutes of wait, another customer rep took over and worked on this case for another 10 minutes or so. At that point, I ended up with two sets of return labels in my email. The customer service rep told me to use the labels from the second email (in chronological order). So the next day, I shipped the replacement Kindle Oasis back. A few days later, I saw on UPS tracking that the package was delivered to Amazon and three days after this I received an email confirmation from Amazon that my first return was received. A few days later, I saw on UPS tracking that the second Kindle Oasis (replacement) was also received by Amazon. I waited a few days for return confirmation and refund from Amazon, but nothing happened. When I contacted Amazon Customer service, they kept telling me that I shouldn't worry about getting charged as my replacement is complete. But they could see no record of my return of the replacement. I spent probably a good half an hour chatting with a customer service rep but they couldn't help me at all since they could only see the record for on return request. That chat ended with no resolution because I ran out of time and had to get to an appointment. Later, I got in touch with yet another service rep, and explained everything from scratch. Luckily, that person was able to find records of both returns being received by Amazon and finally issued me a refund.

So lessons from this story:
1. Don't buy a 9th gen Kindle Oasis. There seems to be serious quality control issues. The probability of one customer receiving two faulty Kindles in a row would be infinitesimal unless fault rates are in the 20% range.
2. If you receive a faulty Kindle from Amazon, return it for a refund. Don't ask for a replacement. Amazon's automated return process cannot handle the return of a replacement unit, and you will sink a lot of time dealing with customer service representatives
text_fidelity_b: Kindle Oasis E-reader (Previous Generation - 9th) – Graphite, 7" High-Resolution Display (300 ppi), Waterproof, Built-In Audible, 32 GB, Wi-Fi - with Special Offers (Closeout)

text_fidelity_a:
Poly - Voyager Focus 2 UC USB-C Headset (Plantronics) - Bluetooth Dual-Ear (Stereo) Headset with Boom Mic - USB-C PC/Mac Compatible - Active Noise Canceling - Works with Teams, Zoom (Certified) & More Ok, so I have to admit at first I was wondering why someone would spend this much on a Bluetooth headset that isn't a feature-rich entertainment one like those from Sony or a major fad brand like Beats, both of which I have some experience with. But this, no... this is actually something different. This is a serious tool for serious use with serious built quality and seriously useful features. Seriously.
For example, the telescoping mouthpiece means you'll get unparalleled mic quality compared to headsets that pick the mic up by your ears (looking at YOU, airpods!), both in clarity and isolation from background noise. You can also physically bend it out of the way, or use the button on the mic itself to mute. Try doing that with airpods. Then there's the button based features. Shortcuts and touch-sensitive buttons are cool on aesthetic devices, but the physical controls on this are an ergonomic user experience DREAM. Everything is easy to access and control, no apps or press-and-hold or counting LED blinks, etc. Sort of makes me miss the old days of phones with physical switches and buttons. When you want your equipment to get serious, this is the sort of user experience you expect. Then there's the charging rack. OMG I love that, I can store it on my desk and it's charging automagically. Pick it up and put it on, ready to go. Never needs to be charged because it's been charging in between uses. Finally, I'm really impressed with the USB dongle option. You see, the one thing I really dislike about wireless headphones is that you usually need to pair it with a device, then unpair it to switch to another device. For example, using my Sony headphones on my phone and tablet, if my wife wants to borrow them for a zoom meeting, I need to pair with her device but then also unpair with mine so that it doesn't keep trying to reconnect to it. Sometimes we just give up and use a wired headset to avoid that mess. Non-bluetooth wireless headsets have a dongle, which makes it easy to swap what you are connected to (no unpairing needed, just move the dongle) but then you can't connect to devices without a USB port like a phone. This is the best of both- you can pair it with your phone, but ALSO use the USB to quickly connect with your desktop or laptop without going through the process of pairing and unpairing. This is the kind of usability and professional quality I would expect from a brand like Plantronics, and all the while it works well as a stereo headset for music/gaming/etc as well. Very comfortable to wear for long hours, I'd highly recommend it for serious users.
text_fidelity_b: Poly - Voyager Focus 2 UC USB-C Headset (Plantronics) - Bluetooth Dual-Ear (Stereo) Headset with Boom Mic - USB-C PC/Mac Compatible - Active Noise Canceling - Works with Teams, Zoom (Certified) & More

text_fidelity_a:
3M Quiet Space Headphones, Bluetooth Headphones, Wireless Headphones, 1 Pair Most of the headphones with which I have worked have been active noise canceling (ANC) phones so I know a lot about those, but I also have other headphones too that I like. I was unaware that 3M even had headphones, and I was also unsure what their "Quiet Space" was all about. It's an interesting solution that works fairly well. Overall, these are good phones, though there's one area that could use some slight improvement and that's the sound profile.

These are over-the-ear phones and they are actually quite comfortable. I like how they feel on my head - they fit snugly and I can tilt my head without losing these phones, but they don't clamp down super tight either.

Build-wise, these are more substantial than the price suggests. I like the size adjustment in particular which is designed to last and should not fatigue with use.

I powered these on and they quickly paired and connected to my laptop. The range is good and I was able to walk a fair distance away without losing the connection or having the sound get crackly or having it skip. With no feed coming to them they eventually powered themselves off, saving battery but potentially frustrating the wearer if this is unexpected.

Just putting these on I was surprised by the amount of noise isolation. Without even turning these on they drastically reduced the ambient noise in the room, even effectively blocking out the sound of a running fan. I have had very few headphones that have as effective sound isolation as these, and that's a huge plus right out of the gate. The Quiet Space function adds to this, but not like ANC phones - it injects white noise into the cans so all you hear is a gentle but constant hiss that overrides most other noises. It's not deathly quiet with these on, but you won't hear most other sounds in the area when they're producing white noise. This is a very different approach to sound cancellation and it works.

The sound profile is the one area where these phones could use a little improvement, though these are not terrible and are better than some big-name phones I have used. The bass is not overdriven but it is not muted either, and this is refreshing since most manufacturers overdrive the bass. The highs are clear, though not shrill. The midrange, however, is flat to the point that music can sound slightly hollow. It's an easy fix with an equalizer and is better than one particular big-name manufacturer's similar flaw.

I like these phones and will be working with them more. They take a different approach to dealing with ambient noise and surrounding distractions than what ANC phones use, and they seem to work well. They're well made, comfortable and reasonably priced.
text_fidelity_b: 3M Quiet Space Headphones, Bluetooth Headphones, Wireless Headphones, 1 Pair

Logitech Optical Trackball Marble Mouse Logitech Trackball Marble Mouse is one of the better computer accessories I have used and it offers a noticeable improvement compared to traditional computer mice. Its unique shape makes it much more comfortable and a no- sliding- necessary design eliminates the need to drag your mouse across a flat surface to move the computer pointer on your screen. To move the pointer, all you do is move the large, red marble trackball. There is less strain on the fingers and wrist, making for a more comfortable experience.

Besides the added comfort, another advantage of the Logitech Trackball Marble Mouse is that it requires less space than a traditional mouse. Because this mouse is stationary and doesn't need to be dragged across a desk or other surface, it can fit into many small spaces. You don't need to make room to drag it, so it can be placed in tight quarters. This is great for those who work in offices with limited desk space.

The Logitech Trackball Marble Mouse offers four buttons to use for clicking. The large tabs on each side of the mouse are used for the usual right and left click functions and then there are two smaller tabs right above each of the larger tabs that are used for various functions. These two small tabs can be programmed to perform several things, and many will likely program them to scroll since this Logitech mouse doesn't have a scroll wheel. But the tabs can be programmed for other things, too. Since I don't necessarily need to scroll, my small tabs have been programmed as browser back and forward buttons. This makes life a little easier because I no longer need to move my mouse to the top of my screen and click the forward and backward arrows in the upper left corner. I just click my small left tab to go back and my small right tab to go forward.

The Logitech Trackball Marble Mouse is a marked improvement compared to the standard mouse, but I admit that it does take some getting used to. Having used a traditional mouse for most of my computer- using years, I had grown accustomed to sliding my mouse across the desk surface. Thus, when I started to use the Logitech Trackball Marble Mouse, I kept sliding it around on my desk also, even though I knew this mouse didn't need to be dragged. It took some time to break this habit. It also took time to get used to the sensitivity of the trackball. The slightest movement sends your pointer flying and when I first started to use this mouse, I would continually underestimate the precision of the Logitech Trackball Marble Mouse. My movements of the trackball were far too extreme. The pointer would soar across my computer screen, even though I would swear I wasn't moving the trackball very much. It is a very sensitive device that almost seems too loose at first because it moves so freely and with such little effort.

Compared to a traditional mouse, the Logitech Trackball Marble Mouse has many great things to offer and it is a mouse I am happy I took the time to try. It is superior to the traditional model in most areas, reducing pain and strain and offering greater accuracy and an easy grip. It does take time to get used to, but it is worth it in the long run and even those who initially resist the change will be happy, in due time, that they made the switch to Logitech.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech Optical Trackball Marble Mouse

Gator Cases 28" Creative Pro Bag for Video Camera Systems with Wheels & Pull Handle (GCPRVCAM28W) Let me start off by saying I work in freelance video and I love how much I can fit inside this case! I've been using a Pelican 1510 as my go-to travel carrier, so that's mostly what I'm comparing this to. For starters, this is a longer case so in addition to my cameras, lenses, batteries and other accessories, it has a long open sleeve that can even fit a light stand or small tripod! For extra versatility, the whole interior can actually be pulled out (it has its own handle straps if you want to use it as its own carrier), which then frees up the ample storage space inside the case as a separate giant unit (see pictures to illustrate). There are also plenty of pockets on the inside, as well as the outside and front of the case. Of course, for a case this size there is the requisite wheels and carrying handle.
The only things I like better about my Pelican case, however, are the toughness and waterproofing. This bag comes with a rain cover which you can keep inside the case, however I don't like the idea of having to carry around a cover inside the bag, then take it out and put it on if it starts raining. The Pelican cases are air tight by simply closing them, no rain cover needed. The Pelican cases also are tough enough that they can be stacked under other equipment, thrown into a corner, sat on, stood on, etc, and 99% of the time come out unscathed. That's more than I can say for this bag. I bring this bag on gigs that I'm not worried about those things happening, because I can fit what I normally take in 3 separate bags into just this one. You could get a Pelican style case in this size, however it would cost quite a bit more than the asking price of this one. I think for the price this is a great tool to keep your stuff organized and ready to go whenever you are!
text_fidelity_b: Gator Cases 28" Creative Pro Bag for Video Camera Systems with Wheels & Pull Handle (GCPRVCAM28W)

1. Very lightweight. It weighs only 4 pounds.
2. Excellent display. It has a full HD screen resolution of 1920x1080. In particular, high resolution digital photos look great on it.
3. Screen size is excellent. It measures a generous 15.6 inches
4. Hard drive is solid state. This makes booting the laptop extremely fast. It is up and running in a mere 30-45 seconds. My previous laptop, which had a mechanical drive, took as much as 10 minutes before it was fully ready to go.
5. Battery charge is good. It lasts up to 7.5 hours.
6. Attractive, modern design. The laptop is slim and sleek, with a lovely, silver color. I especially like the visibility of the backlit keyboard.
7. Excellent price. It offers good value for the cost.

Cons

1. Processing speed is only adequate. Though the speed is probably sufficient for the average user, it could be an issue if you are doing things that require a lot of horsepower, such as editing videos or creating music in digital-audio workstation software.
2. The 4GB of RAM is minimal. This amount of RAM is the very least that any user requires these days. However, it is upgradeable.
3. The hard drive is only 128GB in size. This is a surprisingly small amount for a modern computer. However, it is probably not a problem for the average user.
4. Windows Home "S Mode" may be an issue. It is automatically enabled on the laptop as a security protection for unwary, non-techie users, who might accidentally stray into dangerous territory online that could compromise the laptop. But for the more technically advanced and self-protectively-savvy user, this feature can be very annoying. Fortunately, those same techies can easily figure out how to disable it, which allows the laptop to run the regular Windows Home version.

MavisLink HDMI Cable Fiber Optic 100ft 4K 60Hz HDMI2.0b 18Gbps HDR10 ARC HDCP2.2 YUV4:4:4/4:2:2/4:2:0 Slim Flexible for HDTV/Game Console/Projector/Home Theatre I gave this a four because it did not work on one out of three devices I tried it with (and I know each to work with a short HDMI cable). I'm not sure why this had a lot of flickering when used with my Alienware computer, but it worked perfectly with another computer and my QNAP NAS (worth noting is the NAS puts out a very weak signal and does not work with my in-place 25-ft. traditional HDMI cable).

I had almost written this off because usually HDMI is a crapshoot when it comes to any sort of distance and I didn't even realize such a product existed until I read about fiber optic cable inside. I thought that was a generic brand typo type of situation until I looked this up and realized this is a real thing. I didn't study it, but I gather/assume that there is a chip inside that changes electrical signals to low power lasers to send the signals this way. Interesting, though, because there are not 19 fibers inside (a traditional HDMI cable has 19 pins, I think).

I probably need to research this further just because it's totally cool, but I love this thing because I can now watch my NAS directly on my TV even though it is down in the basement (and there is a great app to act as a remote since I now do not have line of sight for the IR remote). I only took off a star because it apparently has some issues with my one computer - not sure why but if you need a couple of these, you might want to buy one at a time to be sure what it does and does not work with. I love it, but had to remove a star for that reason.

text_fidelity_a:
Echo Dot (2nd Generation) - Smart speaker with Alexa - White So amazing that I bought a second after having the first for a week! The Echo Dot is a smaller version of the Echo. It's small, but mighty and the extra pair of hands every mom has been craving for. Basically the Dot is a computer that you talk to. It's slightly larger than a can of tuna. The Dot has a name. Her name is Alexa, but you can change the name to whatever works best for you. You simply say, "Alexa" and then ask/tell it to do your bidding. What can she do?

Alexa can:
Set multiple timers at once
Set multiple reminders
Add things to your calendar
Tell you time, date, and the weather
Set alarms
Play music from Amazon Prime, Pandora, or Sirius XM
Tell you the news (local, national, or international)
Play radio stations from around the country or the world
Walk you through recipes while cooking
Create shopping lists for when you go to the grocery store
Order products from Amazon
Add products to your Amazon shopping cart
Tell you what is in your shopping cart and order them
Turn on/off lights (if you have the smart bulbs)
Tell you the traffic for your daily commute
and much much more!

The possibilities are endless. I have found getting ready in morning to be easier with the Dot. I don't have to stop and look up the weather. If I need the time, I don't have to find my watch or go into the next room for a clock. I'll know if my regular commute is open or if I need to take an alternative route. Cooking has been less frantic because I just set the multiple timers and I do not have to remember how much time in on the 45 minutes for the ham that I need to take the casserole out. I set the reminders and she just tells me. If want an update on my Amazon purchases, then it's there I do not have to look it up. If I added something to my cart, but forgot to purchase it I can ask Alexa to complete the order. You can play games and you can ask it random questions like How many Super Bowl Rings do the Pittsburgh Steelers have? Or Who was Martin Luther King, Jr.? What is Stargazy Pie?

Downsides? Hardly any, but consider this: The Echo Dot is not made for an awesome stereo listening experience. You can link up bluetooth speakers to it, but while I would say the speaker is great for a bedroom or a kitchen, this is not for your living room/game room/family room. I would advise to get the regular Echo for that. You can link multiple Dots together as well as link a Dot to an Echo, so if you're looking for really good sound that may be the way to go. Also, when I cheerfully tell friends that I have a Dot they retort that it's a listening device and Amazon or the government is listening in on my conversations. They are not. However, if you are really worried, two things, you can turn the microphone off and then Alexa can't "hear" anything or you can unplug the Dot completely. The Echos must be plugged in at all times for them to work. So if you are worried about Amazon executives listening to you while you sleep you can just unplug the entire device when you are not using it. Problem solved. Although no one is actually listening, and if your house is like mine, it's mostly just screaming kids so listen away!

Bottomline: You will not be disappointed!
text_fidelity_b: Echo Dot (2nd Generation) - Smart speaker with Alexa - White

text_fidelity_a:
PreSonus C3.5 BT Channel Studio Monitor I have been wanting to get a bluetooth speaker for connecting to my tablet for a while so I was very pleased to get an opportunity to try this speaker set. It is far and away better than what I originally had in mind and so far I am more than pleased with them.

Setup of these speakers is straightforward and simple, so much so that instructions really are not needed to get started. The wire connector is color-coded to make connecting the speakers to each other almost completely foolproof. If I have any complaints about the setup it would be that the wire connector is a little on the short side but that’s an easy fix - just buy longer wire.

I enabled bluetooth on my tablet, told the speaker set to make itself available and the tablet connected to it immediately. One could not ask for anything simpler. The process took less than a minute and most of that time was spent walking across the room to press the bluetooth button on the speakers.

I loaded up Pandora and told the tablet to play and almost immediately it was clear that these speakers are far above average. The sound profile is stunning - clear and crisp highs, rich midrange and very satisfying bass without overdriving. These speakers do an outstanding job of accurately reproducing the sound. On the back of the main (control) speaker there are two knobs for adjusting the highs and lows should the middle be unsatisfactory for some reason. These speakers also do a good job with spacial elements and there is depth to the sound.

I paired the speakers with my laptop (once I powered off the tablet) as well and it was also very easy.

I took some cables and wired the speakers to an older television in the house to see how much better watching TV would be. It was definitely better and it have a more spacial and stereo sound experience but with our TV this prevented us from making any volume adjustments unless we turned the volume knob on the speaker itself. This is a minor nuisance but certainly not a real issue.

In addition to great sound, these seem to be well-build and rugged, a good sign right out of the box. These are an excellent choice for a home theater system or an audiophile's listening room.

So far I have found nothing about which to complain with these speakers. Set-up is a snap and the sound quality is just amazing. These are speakers for the serious listener.
text_fidelity_b: PreSonus C3.5 BT Channel Studio Monitor

text_fidelity_a:
Amazon Kindle Fire HD 8.9" Standing Leather Case, Fuchsia (will not fit HDX models) This case fits very well and was designed specifically for the Kindle Fire HD 8.9"—with even slick cutouts for the speakers in the back. The Fire just pops right into it and it couldn't be neater or slimmer. The magnetic closure is tidy and holds the case closed quite well. I think Amazon must be trying to recoup some from its bargain-level pricing of its Kindles, however, because I think it's over-priced for what it is (at least at the time of this writing). Still, you can't beat the fit of it.

But a caution is in order for the leather lovers: This may be "genuine leather" but it sure doesn't look or feel like it. If you get it in black or the Saddle Tan, maybe, but the one I was given to review (fuschia) just looks like fancy plastic to me. It has a pebbly texture that makes it easy to hold, but if you want that rich, satisfying feel of well-worn wallet leather, you won't get it with this case. (The Verso Prologue cases have that feel.)

As with so many of the Kindle cases on the market, the inability to clip a stylus to the case is I think an omission. I have a rooCase for my Kindle Fire 7" that I like specifically because I can clip my stylus to the pocket that holds the Kindle. Maybe some hot new designer will come up with a way to design a very slim case that can stow a stylus.
text_fidelity_b: Amazon Kindle Fire HD 8.9" Standing Leather Case, Fuchsia (will not fit HDX models)

text_fidelity_a: Selore&S-Global USB C to Dual HDMI Adapter 4K @60hz, Type C to HDMI Converter for MacBook Pro Air 2020/2019/2018,LenovoYoga 920/Thinkpad T480,Dell XPS 13/15,etc… I’ve had this for 8 months with no issues, then I got an under-the-desk treadmill and the screens go black and immediately come back on ALL THE TIME. I’ve tried using different plug ins for the treadmill and computer, not it (my husband is an electrician and assured me this was not it.). When testing this theory and intentionally removing power and plugging back in, the monitor had a setting box pup-up…. Because it lost powder, great. But when the screen flashes that box doesn’t come up which tells me it’s not loosing power-it’s loosing a connection to the computer. After messing with it and becoming frustrated, I thought I heard a little zap noise where it’s located so when I started feeling around I got a very minor static shock on my finger. So my Inspector Gadget hat told me that I was generating static electricity with my treadmill and for some reason it was collecting on this dual monitor plug and basically shorting itself out. (This only happens when walking on the treadmill.) So, in all my Mom-knowing madness, I wrapped it up in a dryer sheet and it actually works for the most part. It might flash a couple times in a day but my office smells amazing. I will be looking for something else for sure. It’s really annoying.
text_fidelity_b: Selore&S-Global USB C to Dual HDMI Adapter 4K @60hz, Type C to HDMI Converter for MacBook Pro Air 2020/2019/2018,LenovoYoga 920/Thinkpad T480,Dell XPS 13/15,etc…

text_fidelity_a:
Garmin nüvi 1390/1390T 4.3-Inch Bluetooth Portable GPS Navigator (Discontinued by Manufacturer) I first became enamored of the garmin company after using the one with a rental car. The ease of use and accuracy was impressive. Unfortunately, that model is no longer in production so I opted for this unit.

In general I am pleased. Easy to set up, the unit features a bright, clear screen. It is a snap to use and the directions have been unfailing accurate. I drive alot and so far have used this unit throughout New York, New Jersey, Pennsylvania, Maryland, DC and Virginia. I have had no problem with reception even while traversing mountainous regions. I appreciate the advance notice for turns and the voice command system is a convenience.

However, this unit is not flawless. The robotic voice often mispronounces street names and the voice command system seems a bit hard of hearing when it comes to addresses. I have had to pull over and type in the address. The unit does not like to deviate from its chosen route. For instance, one location I frequent in New York is accessible both by the thruway (toll road) and other non-toll main arteries. Both are about the same distance. When I want to avoid the toll route, the unit will recalculate directing that I turn around and follow the initial route multiple times before adjusting to the alternate route. A big deal, no,but annoying nonetheless. While I have not been terribly plagued by the pop ups, they are annoying and potentially unsafe. While the start up guide and manual are adequate, they are barely so. Whatever happened to detailed instructions? But my biggest gripe is the customer service. I called twice with questions and had ridicualously long waits of fifteen minutes and twenty-five minutes respectively. There is no round the clock service. The last time I called it wasnt even available all week, totally unacceptable.

So while I like this system,there is room for improvement.
text_fidelity_b: Garmin nüvi 1390/1390T 4.3-Inch Bluetooth Portable GPS Navigator (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

I bought them because I have a noisy (but lovable) neighbor. The noise cancellation on these is superior, but not for low, bassy, external sounds, but rather sounds in the higher range.

My advise, and to save you some time: Do not get the app. It is so invasive of your information, and I know all apps are, but this one is probably the worst. You can set up bluetooth with all your devices without the app, and use all the features, no problem.

It also has Alexa built in, which is insane, I have yet to pull the trigger on giving Alexa permission, but I think I will; there is an Alexa button, I THINK that's the only time it's listening. If you're like me, and you have Amazon Prime Music the combo is insane.

A few cons: the Noise Cancellation will pound your ears if you’re not listening to content. I didn’t know it could do this, but I can see why people say they can only wear them for so long.

Do not under any circumstance get the app. It’s much more invasive than any app I’ve seen (of tkunborher to read the privacy (publicity) statement. Your earphones can operate fine without the app.

text_fidelity_a:
OTTERBOX DEFENDER iPhone 6 PLUS/6s PLUS Case - Frustration FRĒe Packaging - BLACK This is our fifth OtterBox, dating back to my I phone 3GS. This version has a major improvement,

Pros.
1. The plastic screen finally looks good. There was always a gap between the screen and the I Phone glass. That gave it a cheap look. That gap is gone. The plastic screen goes flush against the I phone glass and looks much better.
2. We have never dropped our phones, but this case gives us a great feeling of security. At $ 800 or so per phone, it's really cheap insurance.

Cons.
1. Installation and removal. We don't install these often enough to remember how to do it. The case comes assembled, and must be disassembled before use. Couldn't remember how to disassemble it. I finally went to You Tube to watch a video. Search term: "installing an OtterBox case." A comment to the video jogged my mind. It's like changing a bicycle tire. I used a miniature screwdriver to separate the rubber from the case at the corner. Nothing sharp. The rest of the rubber came off easily. The plastic parts separated easily enough. Place the phone inside, after cleaning both screens. Click the plastic pieces together, then place the rubber on. Keep massaging the rubber until it fully envelopes the plastic tightly. Had a few gaps at first.

2. Takes away the looks of the I Phone. Steve Jobs must have hated OtterBox.

3. Apple has a neat stand up charger for about $ 35. I bought one. OtterBox was late to the party with the OtterBox 6 plus, so I purchased the Apple 6 Plus leather case. Not much protection, but looks sharp. Worked great with the Apple stand up charger. Looked sharp together. Unfortunately, neither the OtterBox, nor any case that recesses the apple phone insert will work with this charger. Only a very thin shell will work with the charger. Back to using the regular Apple cord. I also have the OtterBox Strada for my I Phone 6. I like it. Although much thinner than the Defender, it doesn't work with the stand up apple charger either. Looks great. Many compliments. For those that don't like to carry a wallet all the time, the Strada has a pocket that contains both my license and one credit card. Great for trips to the gym. My wife has the Defender.
text_fidelity_b: OTTERBOX DEFENDER iPhone 6 PLUS/6s PLUS Case - Frustration FRĒe Packaging - BLACK

TP-Link Deco Mesh WiFi System(Deco M5) –Up to 5,500 sq. ft. Whole Home Coverage and 100+ Devices,WiFi Router/Extender Replacement, Anitivirus, 3-pack This review is for the TP-LInk Mesh WiFi M5 system.
—————
Amended April 28, 2020
Now that I’ve been using this for a couple weeks, I am returning to add these units HAVE NOT cured the dead spots that needed more signal strength. Yes, the WiFi signal is present in those areas of my home. However, the signal strength has not improved over what my centrally located router produced on its own. Essentially for my roughly $125, I got a couple stylish WiFi access points. What I DID NOT GET is the improved coverage promoted in the description.
—————
This IS NOT a plug it in and it works system. You need to know at minimum:
—Your current router’s IP address, the user ID for it, and the password. If you haven’t changed them from the default, you have no business installing a network anything, because you put EVERYTHING on your system at high risk for hacking. Why? The problem is that the default user ID and password are the SAME FOR ALL routers of the same brand (every brand router has a published default user id and password).
—You need to know which of several comm protocols your ISP uses.
—You need to know that IF YOU SWAP OUT YOUR ROUTER for one of the units, the others WILL NOT WORK to extend your WiFi network. For that you need to set these up as extenders, with the first being connected to your existing router.
—To set up a network of WiFi extenders, you need to know how to turn your existing router’s WiFi transmission off. Only then can you use these as extenders, satellites, or whatever you know them as.
—You are highly likely to have to update the firmware on each M5 device.
—You should set aside about two to three hours to set up a network of multiple devices.
—If you set these up as extenders, some of the default security features are switched off. You need to be sure these security features are enabled on your router instead.

I found this an unacceptably under-documented product that forces you to comb through the internet for proper setup tips. I loathe their little booklet that is “documentation” since it is a collection of single pages in multiple languages that direct you to the App Store or Google Play for the app that manages setup. That app is underpowered, has little relevant or helpful information.

I’ve been working with and installing systems from early (1990s) mainframes, Apple IIs, Macs, PCs of all flavors, and networks right up to now. Were it not for that experience, I might never have gotten this to work. Once installed, it works fine.

Recommendation: If your current router is older, you’re probably more likely to get better WiFi coverage by purchasing a newer, more current router. Try that first, and if you don't get the coverage you need, add a couple or three of these.

text_fidelity_a:
Altura Photo Camera Accessories Bundle - Photography Accessories Kit for Canon Nikon Sony DSLR & Mirrorless Cameras, Includes Small Tripod for Camera, Lens Cleaning Kit & Camera Cleaning Kit My daughter and I do a lot of photography of jewelry. We have had a variety of tripods and camera aids. This kit seemed like a good one for us. I got it.

WHAT IS THIS KIT LIKE?
CASE
This has a hard case that zips around the edge. It has a pocket in it to hold things in place and a cupped side to allow for the tripod storage.

LENS BAGS
There are bags in here which fit small medium or large lenses. I don't have any lenses yet, but I do have a small light that fits in one.

CLEANING CLOTH
These come in a zip topped plastic bag. This is pretty nice and works well as is expected with microfiber cloth for cleaning glass.

QUICK RELEASE CAMERA STRAP
This comes in a nice package with good instructions in it. The idea is that this helps stabilize the camera when you are taking a lot of photos. You can not have to grip the camera so hard so your hand does not get tired too. If you accidentally slip your grip, it does not crash to the ground.

This had a learning curve to it, but I finally figured out how to use it for me where it was helpful.

LENS PAPER
This paper allows you to clean the lens off gently wet or dry. The wet means that you use the Altura cleaning solution for greasy heavier prints.

PUFFER CLEANER
This is a rubberized ball that when you squeeze it, there will be a blast of air that will blow things off of the lenses. This works quite well when I get a particle on the lens so I don't have to touch it.

BRUSH
This is when the dust won't blow off the lens or other glass you can gently brush it and then blow it away with the puffer cleaner.

EMPTY BOTTLE
This is for alcohol or lens cleaner.

TRIPOD
This is why I wanted this kit the most. It has an ingenious design to it. It folds up flat and quite small, yet when you take it apart and tilt it, you can stand it up for close photos, or use it in your hand. It has rubber on the bottom to keep it put, and it also has a rubberized grip if you want to hold it. The camera platform tilts, but it locks into place which I love. This is working great for us taking close up photos of some of the small jewelry we are photographing. It has come in really handy.

What I love is that we can pick it up and use it by hand if we need another angle than the table top one.

THE BOTTOM LINE
This kit is a nice kit. I got it mostly for the tripod, but the cleaning accessories and the wrist strap make it really nice. The puffer ball is one of those things that you don't realize you need until you have it.- at least for me. The case is protective and easy to travel with.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. I am happy with this kit. It has worked better for us than I expected. We will be using this a lot in the future too.
text_fidelity_b: Altura Photo Camera Accessories Bundle - Photography Accessories Kit for Canon Nikon Sony DSLR & Mirrorless Cameras, Includes Small Tripod for Camera, Lens Cleaning Kit & Camera Cleaning Kit

Audio-Technica ATH-LS50iSBK In-Ear Monitor Headphones with In-Line Mic & Control, Black As a disclaimer, I'm just an ordinary consumer (vs. a technical expert) when it comes to headphones, speakers, or earbuds. Having said that, here's my experience with these in-ear headphones:

As earbuds go, these are not as lightweight as the much cheaper, AmazonBasics and Panasonic ones I have owned. However, it's a weight difference that isn't really a problem, once I get them securely fastened around my ears.

The sound is wonderful. It has much more clarity than the inexpensive earbuds I usually buy. So to some extent the adage, "You get what you pay for," seems to apply here.

These earbuds have a useful extra: they have a microphone built in. Because of that, you can use it to speak on your cellphone, if you'd rather use this than a Bluetooth. Or if you are listening to entertainment media on your cell phone when you get a call, you won't have to unplug this earbud to take the call.

The microphone control has only one button, an on/off toggle switch. There are no volume adjustment buttons.

These earbuds seem to be well constructed. The cord is thicker and sturdier than my low-cost AmazonBasics and Panasonic earbuds.

The piece that fits into your ear has a relatively large casing compared to my other earbuds, but no doubt this is because the technology is more complicated.

These earbuds are an expensive buy for those of us who normally pay $7-12 for earbuds, but if you like to listen to music, it might be worth it.

PANASONIC Wings Sport Headphones are Ultra-Light Wireless Bluetooth Sport Earbud 3D Flex Sport Clips with Microphone and Call/Volume Controller, IPX5 Rated Water-Resistant - RP-BTS35-K (Black) These headphones don't really hit the mark for me -- maybe because I have a small head and smaller ears. They stay on and don't fall off even when running but I can't get the fit correct where the driver stays sealed in my ear the way its supposed to (tried all sets of tips included). When they come loose the sound quality is very bad since these are a sealed design headphone and rely on creating a seal with your inner ear to reproduce low frequencies, so they sound very tinny and harsh. Even when I use my fingers to hold the drivers in place though, the sound quality of these is pretty mediocre compared to my other sony BT headphones.

Also when I tighten the band in the back to prevent cable noise when running, that makes the control pod be on the back of my neck which is kind of awkward to use. I also don't like the overall design which looks and feels kind of bulky, at least they are pretty light weight though. These headphones worked as expected and had no issues with syncing, if they fit better I would have given them 3 or 4 stars but I have a pair of sony bluetooth headphones that sound better, fit better, and look better for about the same cost so I really can't recommend these.
text_fidelity_b: PANASONIC Wings Sport Headphones are Ultra-Light Wireless Bluetooth Sport Earbud 3D Flex Sport Clips with Microphone and Call/Volume Controller, IPX5 Rated Water-Resistant - RP-BTS35-K (Black)

text_fidelity_a:
ONANOFF Fokus Headphones, Premium Concentration Over-Ear Headphones, Designed with Two Unique Listening Modes: FokusMode and MusicMode, Adjustable, Built-in Mic, and Passive Noise Cancellation, Grey I'm so happy to see they are still making new brands of wired headphones... lately all the new designs and features have been found in wireless only, and sometimes I just want a good pair of wired 'phones, especially for use with my Quad-DAC headphone jack.
They are passive noise cancelling, which basically just means they cushion sound out mechanically with nice big ear muff style rings, as opposed to any kind of digital reverse-sine-wave trickery (which are hit or miss on cheap brands usually), and it has a really interesting "focus" mode switch, which changes the EQ of the mix to promote the frequencies used in spoken words better. This is an amazing feature for those of us who listen to audiobooks or lectures, which I do frequently. To be honest, I didn't notice a big difference between having that mode on and off, but it was nice to know someone out there is trying to make products catered for people who want to do more than just listen to music over Bluetooth.
The sound quality is pretty good for the price, and the presentation is actually really impressive. The materials feel really premium and even the box it comes in feels super fancy, which might make this a nice gift. I don't expect much out of mics that are embedded in headphones, and this pair didn't change my mind about that. The mic isn't close enough to your mouth to be of much use, picking up more ambient noise around you than you. If they wanted to include that as a feature, they could have made a removable arm like a gaming headset, but they don't need to. This is a good pair of headphones for those of us who just want to listen, which is their ideal demographic IMO.
text_fidelity_b: ONANOFF Fokus Headphones, Premium Concentration Over-Ear Headphones, Designed with Two Unique Listening Modes: FokusMode and MusicMode, Adjustable, Built-in Mic, and Passive Noise Cancellation, Grey

text_fidelity_a:
bopmen Headset with Microphone - Computer PC Headset with Boom Mic, in-line Volume Control & Mute, On Ear Wired Headphones for Skype, Home, Office, Classroom, Call Center, Black (S100) I got this for my teenaged son to use on his gaming PC. He had actually broken his previous gaming headphones and this seemed like a no-frills decent replacement for him to try.
The sound quality is actually quite good. Both the ear pieces and the microphone are crisp and clear, so no complaints there. However my son found it a little uncomfortable to wear compared to his larger over-the-ear style headphones before. The actual ear parts on this are smaller, which means they don't fully envelop your ears the way other ones do. On the plus side, this means it doesn't block as much external noise, which I like for him in our household (no more calling his name when he can't us!), but others may want more noise isolation. Also, the smaller ear pieces aren't as comfortable when worn as the larger ones.
I also didn't like that it didn't come with an adapter to break out for mic and speakers like other headsets do. I thought it would come with that as an option, as I've never gotten a PC headset that didn't offer either a splitter or TRRS combo adapter so you can use it with both a laptop that has mic/headphone combos as well as separate mic and headphone jacks commonly found on a desktop.
Thankfully I had an extra one lying around for him to use, so that wasn't an issue. But something to take into consideration. Others, I've got to give it at least 4 stars for working well and doing what it should. But there might be other options for the price worth considering as well if you want larger earphones or a breakout cable included.
text_fidelity_b: bopmen Headset with Microphone - Computer PC Headset with Boom Mic, in-line Volume Control & Mute, On Ear Wired Headphones for Skype, Home, Office, Classroom, Call Center, Black (S100)

text_fidelity_a: Dericam PTZ WiFi IP Security Camera,1080P Surveillance CCTV Outdoor Camera, Pan/Tilt/Zoom, 4X Optical Zoom, Night Vision, Motion Detection, IP65Weatherproof Pre-Installed 32G SD Card, Black I got two outdoor security cameras of different brands at the same time.  The other brand I could not get to work and setting it up was complicated and could apparently only be done through a cell phone.  This camera, on the other hand, could be set up with a computer and the setup was easy and I had it working within minutes, for a live feed.  The picture quality is good and I tested in the dark and still got a great picture.  I didn't give it 5 stars because I couldn't get it to record (supposedly it has some built-in memory, although you can also add a memory card for more memory).  For ease of setup and for the live feed, I give it 5 stars.  I'll try to work with it some more and if I get all the features working, will update this review.  Important note:  I got this without giving thought to the fact that I didn't have a good place to mount it outside.  Also, it needs an outlet to be plugged into, as do most security cameras.  I have outside outlets, but nothing up near the roof where I would want to mount this.  The power cord is not long enough to go for a very great distance, so might require an extension cord to run it.  An exposed extension to a security camera is not very secure, as all anyone would need to do is unplug it to disable the camera.  I thought perhaps I could just keep it inside and aim it out of a window.  Unfortunately my windows sills are two narrow for the camera to sit and shoot out of a window.  I didn't find a good way yet to mount in front of a windows.  Of course my lack of planning is no fault of the camera.  The camera seems rugged and well built.  It appears to be able to use 5Ghz Wi-Fi; the other camera I tested did not.  There is one slight design flaw; the aerial is very close to the mounting bracket, so it is difficult to position it properly.
text_fidelity_b: Dericam PTZ WiFi IP Security Camera,1080P Surveillance CCTV Outdoor Camera, Pan/Tilt/Zoom, 4X Optical Zoom, Night Vision, Motion Detection, IP65Weatherproof Pre-Installed 32G SD Card, Black

text_fidelity_a:
Vizio VAP430 Co-Star Streming Media Client (Black) I really want to like the Co-Star, but it's just not there yet.

Pros
* Simple - Easy to set up and use.
* Remote - Other than the delay mentioned in cons, the remote performs beautifully.
* UI - Vizio did a great job altering the stock Google TV UI.

Cons
* Connectivity - The device doesn't seem to want to stay connected to my WiFi. It also doesn't always auto-reconnect when it loses the signal. It's worked great ever since I started using a Cat5 cable instead.
* Apps - The App store is filled with mostly terrible apps at the moment. I was excited about the Amazon app, but it literally just launches the Amazon webpage. Really Amazon!?!?!
* Blocked content - This isn't an issue with the device, as much as content providers' reaction to it. Major content sites like Comedy Central and Hulu have blocked Google-TV. This can be fixed by altering the user-agent in advanced Chrome settings, but 1) that leads to a desktop site that's harder to navigate and 2) most people won't know to do that.
* Flash player - Again, this isn't necessarily an issue with the device, but Flash tends to crash or run very slowly on it.
* Delayed input - The remote seems to have a 0-1 second processing delay (normally closer to 0), but this leads to you double pressing buttons and ending up in the wrong place.

I would rate the experience much lower than my media center PC and about on par with Roku II (which I also think is flawed).
text_fidelity_b: Vizio VAP430 Co-Star Streming Media Client (Black)

text_fidelity_a:
BRAINWAVZ S0 in-Ear Earbuds Noise Isolating Earphones Clearwavz Remote & Microphone Stereo Headphone Headset for iPhone iPad, iPod & Android Devices (Black) Since there are some incredibly detailed and helpful reviews already I will focus on where these phones are best suited. I received mine as a review sample and have been using them for nearly a week to make sure I thoroughly test them.

For me these are best for critical listening, and especially raw mixes if you do recording. Of course they are not limited to that. The fact that these phones are fairly neutral across the entire frequency spectrum makes them ideal for listening to unmixed recordings, as well as music that you are studying or transcribing. The reproduction is so balanced that listening to albums with these compared to other phones - including some other Brainwavz models - is like night and day.

If you are listening to music that is heavily biased towards bass and drums these may not be the best phones for you. If you listen to acoustic music these are near perfect because you can easily hear every note. I tested it on a few jazz albums that I own as well as a broadcast of two friends from a local station that had been recorded directly from the sound board and it was wonderful to hear what was actually recorded versus what a biased pair of phones normally reproduce.

A few notes about comfort: these are light, do a great job of isolating ambient noise without totally eliminating it, and are easy to wear. I am not an IEM (in ear monitor) type of person, but these presented no problems even when I wore them for three to four hours straight. A big plus is this set comes with different sized foam ear pieces and a nice case (the [[ASIN:B00HPPL1M4 Brainwavz Hard Earphone Case]]).

While these phones may not be for everybody, they are perfect for those of us who spend a lot of time critically listening to music and/or transcribing it. If you fall into that category you will probably love them.
text_fidelity_b: BRAINWAVZ S0 in-Ear Earbuds Noise Isolating Earphones Clearwavz Remote & Microphone Stereo Headphone Headset for iPhone iPad, iPod & Android Devices (Black)

Fitness Tracker, Blood Oxygen & ECG Apps, Always-On Retina Display, Water Resistant I got a lemon. The watch was dead on arrival. No “C” charger is included so I had to buy one for $17. I don’t understand why Apple doesn’t include one in the package. I would be happy to pay an extra $17 for the watch with a charger included. You can’t use this watch without a charger. The watch has been on the charger all night and it is still dead. I am returning. Now I have to wait for UPS to pick it up from my house. There is no drop off option. Then I have to wait 7 -14 days for a refund. Overall this has been a bad experience.

It took 2 weeks and several conversations to get a refund from Amazon. At the time of purchase I ordered the Apple Care package. They did not automatically refund the price of Apple Care for the dead watch. To get a refund I had to be transferred to another department. I was told that Amazon doesn’t refund digital orders. But, because of the circumstances they would give me a full refund. So, if you buy the watch, and purchase Apple care you will NOT automatically get a refund for Apple care if you change your mind.

I purchased this watch on sale at Costco. I feel much better knowing that I can return it directly to the store
If I have a problem.

Time Warner online activation communicated with the modem but then failed. This sent me to activation support where a polite lady in India wasted an hour of my time. Finally I got through to "level 3 tech support" and my modem was activated in less than 5 minutes. The issue was because the modem had been registered to a previous owner (refurbished -- duh!) and the activation needed a lvl 3 tech authorization to move it from one account to the next (kicker is that it was likely TWC who sold these refurbs in the first place!).
Please learn from my mistake, try the online activation if you like but if it fails after already recognizing your new modem (step 2), give up and call TWC "level 3 tech support." Make sure you have the MAC # which is on the bottom of the modem.
Or if you have any alternative to TWC then do yourself a solid and switch providers.

text_fidelity_a:
Linksys N300: Wi-Fi Wireless Router, Linksys Connect, Parental Controls, Home Internet, Wireless Devices up to 300 Mbps Transfer Speed (Black) I've been using a Linksys router for years and it never missed a beat (their wireless G model with the two antennas). But, after upgrading my Internet from DSL to cable, I thought a new router would be in order.

Before buying one I searched for reviews from computer and tech magazines/sites. Talk about confusing! I'd read one review that gave a sterling endorsement for a particular router; then another review from another site that gave the same router a horrible review.

Since my router needs are pretty basic (just use it to share Internet access) I concentrated on ease of install issues. In that regard there was consensus about how easy Linksys is to install. So I went with them again, and selected the 1200 model since it gave me all that I wanted/needed at a good price (but, to hedge my bets, I got it at a warehouse club so I could return it easily).

So happy with this router! Installation was SO simple -- if you can plug in a cable you can install this router. But, should you want to tinker with settings, you can also access the full, detailed configuration menu and tweak settings to your heart's content. I think it took me longer to open up the box and unwrap the router and power cord than it took to actually get it to work.

Performance so far has been excellent. I put it on the ground level of my house and have no problems getting a strong signal in the basement and upper level. I did find that it helps to put the router in the middle of the house rather than against a wall for best signal strength throughout the house.

Considering that my Linksys G is still cranking along after several years, I'm reasonably confident (or at least hopeful) that this will last me an equal length of time.

If you're looking for a solid, easy to install single band router, this is it. Highly recommend.
text_fidelity_b: Linksys N300: Wi-Fi Wireless Router, Linksys Connect, Parental Controls, Home Internet, Wireless Devices up to 300 Mbps Transfer Speed (Black)

text_fidelity_a:
MOOLINK WiFi Digital Photo Frame, 1920 * 1200 Full HD Display, 1080P Digital Picture Frame, 10.1 inch Touch Screen, 16GB Storage, Share Photos via App or Email, Smart WiFi Electronic Picture Frame I love technology, but I can't navigate new tech as easily as I used to. I fear that I'm turning into my parents, who needed my help with programming the VCR. These days, everything seems to have software that you must navigate, and it is seldom as intuitive as it once was for me.

This frame was easy to figure out, though, at least for the features I care about. I skipped right over the parts where it wanted to connect to my network and so forth. I just wanted to upload photos from a micro-SD card, and then have it play them back to me. And it does that very well.

It has a light sensor that adjusts the brightness of the screen automatically if you enable it to, which is a very nice feature that is lacking on my other digital picture frames. I was also able to program it to go to sleep when I'm never up, to save on energy. I didn't want it to be motion activated, as I want it to be displaying photos the moment I walk into the room. Fortunately, this feature is already off by default.

The frame looks really nice, with a small "mat" border around the display. This mat is something that most digital frames are lacking, and let me tell you, this tiny feature makes a huge difference. It really sells the idea that this is a picture frame, instead of merely a digital display. I can't say enough about how much this improves the aesthetic of this frame.

I have a couple of digital frames that I use in a horizontal orientation, so I deleted all my vertical photos from them and moved them onto this one instead, and set it up in a vertical orientation. It is so nice to have the frame matched to the orientation of the photos! You don't get those huge bars on the sides or top/bottom, or if you have it set to crop then you don't crop out 2/3 of the photo!

I have no complaints about this digital photo frame. I can't speak for all of the features, because I have no use for some of them. But the features I wanted work great, and the frame itself looks fantastic!
text_fidelity_b: MOOLINK WiFi Digital Photo Frame, 1920 * 1200 Full HD Display, 1080P Digital Picture Frame, 10.1 inch Touch Screen, 16GB Storage, Share Photos via App or Email, Smart WiFi Electronic Picture Frame

text_fidelity_a: Western Digital 4TB WD Blue PC Internal Hard Drive HDD - 5400 RPM, SATA 6 Gb/s, 256 MB Cache, 3.5" - WD40EZAZ The price of these is usually low enough to consider buying them new for off-line storage. Something most people don't consider using a hard drive for. 4TB has become small for my purposes, but as off-line storage I don't want to risk more than that on one drive. It's much simpler to archive data on a 4TB hard drive in a dock and keep it in a case than to burn 4TB to a stack of Blu-Ray disks every few months, and DVDs are completely out of the question. I'm archiving around 20TB of 4K video that I've captured with GoPros so far. Most of it is on "retired" drives, but I've run out of reliable older drives and I think I'll be upgrading to these in the future. They're unlikely to store data forever without some degradation, but rewriting the data once a year won't wear them out for decades. These will not work well in an NAS or even a RAID array in a PC, and shouldn't be used in a PC with more than one or two hard drives anyway. They're not designed to cope with vibration from several other drives, but as a single drive or for data backup they're fine. It's a capable drive for typical home use. For full-time use in an array, the Red Plus and Red Pro drives are what I get. If you need to store large amounts of data off-line, or if you just need a new drive in a home PC, this is a good choice.
text_fidelity_b: Western Digital 4TB WD Blue PC Internal Hard Drive HDD - 5400 RPM, SATA 6 Gb/s, 256 MB Cache, 3.5" - WD40EZAZ

text_fidelity_a:
Shure AONIC 215 Wired Sound Isolating Earbuds, Clear Sound, Single Driver, Secure In-Ear Fit, Detachable Cable, Durable Quality, Compatible with Apple & Android Devices - Blue Unboxing: Wouldn't usually make a section of this, but every once in a while a product makes it a pleasure. Especially a weird one like this. It's like unboxing a little UFO. It starts out in something like a hat box with a couple sticky tabs of tape to remove. Wish they could have found a better closure method, but the box is nice. Inside that you're immediately presented with the odd looking earbuds and a starter guide (also round) that has you immediately trying them on and fitting the best sleeve size for in your ear. There are no extra sleeves obviously apparent, so time to dig deeper. Next up is the UFO. A large earbud like this needs a large charging case. This one is round and unzips like some of the nicer headphone cases, but it's also a hard case with lights and buttons. Nothing inside but a charging dock. Under it is a secret compartment (made less secret by the thumb holes for easy removal). At the bottom of the hat box we have our missing sleeves and a charging cord.

Even with a diagram, putting these on was confusing and took four tries. Once they're on though, they are quite comfortable, and I think I'll learn to put them on after a few more tries.

Back to the book, and ugh! now they're telling me to put them in the charging case to pair. But I just finally got them on! &*^@#!

Ok, after getting things paired and back on, I'm able to put them through some testing. I'm not really an audiophile, but I've tried a lot of earbuds. Comfort is good. They don't rely on being stuck in your ear to hold themselves up, so there isn't a high stress point that's going to get sore first. They sound good. Better than most, but not the best I've heard. The control button is on the back of your ear, and I find it awkward and unreliable. Noise cancellation is solid, but like every other one I've tried, it is hard to tell sometimes because it scales with volume. Turning them on in a noisy room doesn't result in a quiet room, but turning up what you are listening to will result in noise other than what you are listening to disappearing quite a lot. There is a passthrough mode if you need to hear what's going on around you, but it doesn't sound very nice.

I like that it's USB-C. No more having to turn the cord over three times to figure out which end is up, and much faster charging. The case has three lights to show you charge progress for the case Each one represents enough charge for one full use of the earbuds. There's also a light on the top to tell you whether the earbuds are charged yet.

It's a solid product. Not my top favorite, but definitely innovative and a competitive offering.
text_fidelity_b: Shure AONIC 215 Wired Sound Isolating Earbuds, Clear Sound, Single Driver, Secure In-Ear Fit, Detachable Cable, Durable Quality, Compatible with Apple & Android Devices - Blue

text_fidelity_a:
Native Union Night Cable - 10ft Ultra-Strong Reinforced [MFi Certified] Durable Lightning to USB-A Charging Cable with Weighted Knot Compatible with for iPhone 14, iPhone 13 and Earlier (Cosmos) There are two of us in the house that use iPhones with the lightning port and as such we do need extra cables. Lightning cables are great but they do have a tendency to break. Also, not all third-party cables are the same and some are not worth the box they ship in. I was anxious to try this cable and I have found it to be a perfectly acceptable replacement for the one that came with my phone. Actually, it’s better.

First things first - it is important to note that this cable is MFI-certified which is actually a big deal. I have worked with cables that are certified and those that are not. Those that carry certification are guaranteed to work properly with your device, while those that are not certified are a roll of the dice. This cable is certified so it means two things you can expect from it: it will allow you to charge your phone without worry, and it will allow you to connect your phone to your computer without complaining about the cable being unauthorized. It just works.

The cable is shielded in a heavy nylon weave and that is a double-edged sword. On one hand it means the cable is very stiff and not very bendy which may or may not be an issue. More importantly, though, it means it is going to last longer than plastic coated cables which tend to flex and break.

The ends are terminated well too, with a hard plastic sleeve at the end of each plug where the cable connects. This spot is where most cables fail, and it is nice to see that some thought was put into reinforcing the cable at this point.

The weighted ball is interesting but to me it gets in the way. It can be slid up and down the cable which has its uses, but it is large enough and bulky enough to be more of a hindrance to me than a help. That said, if you are putting this cable in an area where it will not be moved and you intend to leave it there for the long term, it does prevent tangles and it allows for keeping gently tension on the cable.

Overall, I am pleased with this cable. It’s a lot less expensive than Apple-branded cables and it definitely is more durable and should last a long time.
text_fidelity_b: Native Union Night Cable - 10ft Ultra-Strong Reinforced [MFi Certified] Durable Lightning to USB-A Charging Cable with Weighted Knot Compatible with for iPhone 14, iPhone 13 and Earlier (Cosmos)

Logitech HD Webcam C525, Portable HD 720p Video Calling with Autofocus - Black [[VIDEOID:132a9e1a9608d7ddcfd6e870320f72aa]] The 75 second video is intended as a supplement to the written review so that you can see for yourself how well my fairly standard computer can record 720p, and thus get an idea if your computer can benefit from a 720p recording device. This is important to consider because even the manufacturer mentions that many computers cannot keep up with the recording. I mention my system specs in the video.

It's a well designed webcam. It is very small, and the ability to protect its own lens is great. They supply ~5 ft. cord that - wrapped up - takes up about as much room as the camera itself, which allows a connection between a desktop and a separate monitor. Better would have been if they used a standard micro USB connector or some kind of cord wrap system to keep all that out of your way and allow you to use a 30cm cord for connection to your laptop.

The actual optics seem great and the autofocus works pretty well. Even Win XP SP2 allowed me to use the camera function (no video) immediately without installing any software. The software that comes with it eats up nearly 300MB of ROM (that includes their own calling application and editing software that you don't need to install) and only tries caducously to take over your computer (a registry edit and startup menu delete gets rid of unwanted reminders and useless junk running in the background). Oh...I noticed one typo in their software, which is unacceptable, and it also keeps telling me that it doesn't recognize the mic (which is built into the camera), but it records sound anyway.

The design allows for mounting on a monitor 26mm thick or less, but I suppose you could sort of lay it on top of a CRT monitor with no problems. It also allows for a fairly stable mounting on a laptop.

Great device that I would recommend, but I had to take off a star for less than perfect portability and some software blips.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech HD Webcam C525, Portable HD 720p Video Calling with Autofocus - Black

If you are looking for a mouse that is functional, doesn't cost a lot, you aren't using it for gaming, and you can lighten your touch, then this is for you. It isn't going to withstand rough usage. Constructed of water repellant nylon inside and out, this bag is impeccably stitched, has sturdy zippers that work flawlessly, a comfortable carry handle, and offers plenty of storage. In fact, the pack can hold two laptops up to 17" at the same time along with other gear.

Here's the layout:

Front - a 10" x 9" side opening zippered compartment, a 12" x 16" zippered compartment with 2 sleeves for cell phone, battery bank etc, 2 pen holding sleeves, plus a 10" x 4" zippered mesh compartment.

Sides - 4.5" x 7" beverage holders on each side that are large enough to accommodate even larger bottles and sit flush when not being used.

Main Compartment - double zipper provides entry and can be locked to prevent theft. Inside are two cell phone/gadget pouches, an 8" x 6" zippered compartment, and a 12" x 11" laptop or tablet sleeve with no padding on the front. I was able to fit my 15" Lenovo ThinkPad into this sleeve with room to spare and although the sleeve front isn't padded, the entire compartment t is surrounded with excellent padding. Rear - comfortable padded carry handle, the back unzips to reveal a large well padded compartment that can fit up to a 17" laptop. Straps - thickly padded, mesh lined, and ergonomically curved, with a sunglasses loop on one side. The adjustment hardware is heavy duty plastic that functions smoothly and all of the stress points are well reinforced.

This is a very well designed laptop bag made of excellent materials that should be durable. It would function well for school, business, or travel, and it seems very reasonably priced considering the quality.

This backpack was provided at no cost for evaluation purposes.

ULANZI T2 Adjustable Tablet Holder for Desk, Carbon Steel Tablet Stand for Bed, Flexible Tablet Arm Clamp Compatible with iPad Pro, iPad Air, iPad Mini, Galaxy Tab, iPhone & 4.6-12.9 Inch Devices I wanted to use the ULANZI T2 Adjustable Tablet Holder to suspend my iPad Air 4 over my bed. I’ve already tried using a gooseneck holder to hold my iPad, but it was wobbly and every time I moved, the iPad bounced. So I thought the spring-loaded design of this one would prevent wobbling.

There are no assembly instructions inside the box. It’s not rocket science, but I shouldn’t have to look at the product page to figure out how to put it together. Instructions would also be helpful to show all the adjustability options for the various angles.

The mounting clamp only has a usable opening of 1¾ inches, so I’d advise double checking the width of where you want to mount it. I have a desk beside my bed that I used to mount the tablet holder, and I lucked out that the front of the desk didn’t have a metal frame underneath it. Otherwise, it wouldn’t have fit.

The tablet holder part held my iPad Air, with my iPad in a thin TPU case. The sides of the tablet holder have silicone pads (the clamp does too) to prevent scratching the tablet. But the grips aren’t too deep, so they won’t accommodate a thick case or device.

Unfortunately, this metal tablet holder had the same problem as the gooseneck one: it’s wobbly. It starts out okay, but I have to keep tightening the various screws, or my iPad wobbles. I also feel like it’s unsteady when stretched to the maximum length, so that impacts how I have to position the tablet holder.
text_fidelity_b: ULANZI T2 Adjustable Tablet Holder for Desk, Carbon Steel Tablet Stand for Bed, Flexible Tablet Arm Clamp Compatible with iPad Pro, iPad Air, iPad Mini, Galaxy Tab, iPhone & 4.6-12.9 Inch Devices

text_fidelity_a:
Jabra Evolve 40 MS Professional Wired Headset, Mono – Telephone Headset for Greater Productivity, Superior Sound for Calls and Music, 3.5mm Jack/USB Connection, All-Day Comfort Design, MS Optimized These headphones are the most comfortable I have ever owned. The ear cups sit flat against the ear, which feels more natural than the usual headphone with ear cups that surround your ear with a hot and sweaty dome. I could only handle that style for a while and then my ears needed a cool off to dry out. If you are using these headphones somewhere loud, like a train stop, the environment noises will interfere a bit, same if you turn the volume up bystanders will hear it. But the lack of hot and sweaty ears is such a bonus so these other problems are easily avoided.

The headphones are instantly compatible with all smartphones with a headphone jack. I used it on a Google Pixel and on iPhone 5's the sound quality was crystal clear, much better than any bluetooth headset I've ever had, and I've had plenty.

The USB adapter with the call controls worked great for my business calls GoToMeeting, Skype for Business and Google Voice.

The cord is three feet long, perfect for me since I get tired of getting the cord tangled as I pace around during calls, but it might be a bit on the short side for some. For use with the computer the USB adds two feet between the USB port and the controlling buttons. The cord is round, and so far, has been resistant to kinks.

The volume and mute buttons are on the cord instead of the headset, I like this because I don't have to memorize the placement during a call and the indicator light for mute keeps me from forgetting that I have muted a call and no one can hear me because I muted to sneeze, cough or shush my cat.

The only drawback is that unlike with a bluetooth headset there are no volume or mute controls as part of the headset or cord when it is plugged into a smart phone.
text_fidelity_b: Jabra Evolve 40 MS Professional Wired Headset, Mono – Telephone Headset for Greater Productivity, Superior Sound for Calls and Music, 3.5mm Jack/USB Connection, All-Day Comfort Design, MS Optimized
