text_fidelity_a:
Sony ICFS79W AM/FM/Weather Band Digital Tuner Shower Radio (White) FM reception is flat out horrible where I live. It's like a radeo dead zone. My home theater system can pull in nothing. My stereo gets a lot of static. I listen almost exclusively online but I'd heard good things about this radio so I decided to give it a try. The reception was amazing. Perfectly clear. No static on FM at all. It sounds beautiful. The weather feed was full of static, but servicable--I ususally can't pull in the weather band at all. AM is average--neither the worse I've heard nor the best. But then, I don't expect much from AM.

It does the FM1, FM2 trick that some cars do. There is no difference. It just lets them repurpose the buttons. I find it odd, but not bad.

The only think I would have changed is how it hangs. If you don't have a shower hook (I don't) it hangs over the shower head. That tilts the entire unit forward. It should either suspend from the shower curtain rack (the strap is oriented the wrong way to do that--it would try to hand perpendicular to the curtain) or reach a better balance point. That's an issue of aesthetics, not function. I'd be worried about sitting it on the edge of the tub, as it is too likely to fall.

The one trick to remember, when sticking the antenna to the shower wall, is that suction cups don't work as well on a wet surface. Thoroughly dry the wall first, then place it. It helps will the issue of the antenna falling.
text_fidelity_b: Sony ICFS79W AM/FM/Weather Band Digital Tuner Shower Radio (White)

text_fidelity_a:
Fire Tablet with Alexa, 7" Display, 16 GB, Blue - with Special Offers (Previous Generation - 5th) This tablet was purchased to replace my 85 year old mother's Big Lots special that she used for years and which was starting to have more problems than it was worth. The biggest problem my mother had was adjusting to the wide-screen 16:9 format of the Fire tablet compared to the old fashioned 4:3 format of her old tablet. This also had a faster processor with two more cores and four more megs of ram augmented by an 8gb memory card to expand storage. The blue color is quite attractive. The tablet so far runs everything she wants and I've even taught her to use the appstore to download her favorite games. The colors are sharp and clear. Video is smooth and while we watched only one half hour show so far there was no pausing or buffering.
I think the only thing I honestly dislike and it's my fault for not seeing it when this was a Prime Day special. I can forgive the tablet going out of stock and not being alerted to that fact when we placed the order. What I find somewhat insulting is this is the ONLY Fire tabled that comes with a limited 90 day warranty while every other Fire tablet has a minimum of one year warranty. I think there's something wrong with that. I probably would have bought this anyhow. My mom can't stand the weight of my 10" tablet (an ounce heavier than the 10" Fire) and the 8" was (and still is) available in one configuration (color, memory, special offers, etc.) which wasn't attractive and appeared to be fairly heavy.

text_fidelity_a:
Apple 12.9-inch iPad Pro Wi-Fi + Cellular - 12.9" Tablet - 256 GB - 3G/4G - GOLD There is so much talk about the declining sales of iPad. So much so, the discussion might influence a potential buyer to pause before buying or not buy at all, and instead buy a competing tablet or laptop. I think the key to making a decision to buy the iPad Pro lies in a wallpaper Apple provided with the very first version of iPad. It was a licensed photograph of Pyramid Lake by Robert Misrach. The exposure, made at night, appears to be in daylight. The clue that it was a night time photograph are the star trails that resulted from the long exposure. The lake surface appears as smooth as a mirror. The mirror surface of the lake in this photograph enables the viewer to immerse himself or herself in the device, making it a perfect fulfillment of whatever there desires might be "for iPad". The iPad is a perfect "evocative object", evoking whatever feelings and intentions the iPad user brings to it. That is why the iPad is so undefinable and uncategorizable. It is is whatever ever we want it to be.....and with iPad Pro Apple reaches again for that elusive quality.

After 7 days with the new Apple iPad Pro I am happy that I followed my hunch that the iPad Pro would be better for me than a laptop for a mobile multi-purpose device. I am very pleased how the slide over multitasking works. Bigger is better whether using multi-tasking features live slide over and picture-in-picture. The user does not get poorly sized Windows for both applications. For example if your browser is open in one window, and photos is open in a second, but applications are scaled to size in each window.

I purchased the 32MB version because I tend to use iCloud to store photos, music, documents. I only need local storage for IOS apps and the few documents I need.

I purchased a black rear cover, and a contrasting white front cover. The only accessory I use so far is the Apple Pencil for drawing in Paper by 53 and Apple Notes ( to take notes in my University classes ). I use the iPad Pro almost exclusively landscape or horizontal, the only iPad that can be used in portrait is the Mini. At the time I purchased the iPad Pro the wait times for shipment of the Apple Pencil was 4-5 weeks. However, I was able to find one locally at my University Bookstore. I am concentrating on using the Apple Pencil at the moment, using just the on-screen keyboard. I have an open mind about buying the iPad Pro keyboard in the future. However, the iPad is all about creating art through use of touch and the pencil right now. I don't want it to be a laptop. I want it to be a "blank sheet of paper".

The audio produced by the 4 speakers produce a very pleasing music listening experience without headphones.

One final note: it appears the iPad Pro includes technology that can be used in the future today's blog post in Daring Fireball notes that the Lightning connector includes support for USB 3.0, a much faster transfer speeds. It will be interesting to see what applications take advantage of that speed next year.
text_fidelity_b: Apple 12.9-inch iPad Pro Wi-Fi + Cellular - 12.9" Tablet - 256 GB - 3G/4G - GOLD

text_fidelity_a:
Tiffen 82VND 82 Millimeter Variable ND Filter Shooting video outdoors with a DSLR requires, obviously, proper exposure. When shooting at 24 (23.978) frames per second, the normal shutter speed should be 1/50th of a second (1/60 at 29.97 fps). If the camera is set at the lowest ISO rating of 100, in bright daylight the f/stop would be around f/22. If you want to operate at wider aperture to achieve shallow depth of field, you need to cut the light.

This variable density filter allows such an adjustment. The problem is that it cuts the light by rotating two polarizing filters against each other. Polarizers can be tricky and, by design, modify the quality of light. Thus it may act unexpectedly.

One downside is that the front of the filter is not threaded and my 77mm model is a larger diameter than the 70-200mm Nikon zoom it fits on. So now the bayonet lens hood won't fit. Now I'm outdoors with a filter on the lens and no hood to block flare. There aren't any hoods that naturally fit the filter so you need to tape a hood to the outer ring or use a matte box.
text_fidelity_b: Tiffen 82VND 82 Millimeter Variable ND Filter

Crucial X6 4TB Portable SSD - Up to 800MB/s - PC and Mac - USB 3.2 USB-C External Solid State Drive - CT4000X6SSD9 Crucial is one of the first names that comes to mind when I have needed reliable RAM for my systems in the past. I have a Crucial 500MB SSD in one of my systems and it has served me well over the years so I was interested in this SSD as a back-up option for pictures and data. It has proven to be a fine solution for my needs.

Right up front – yes, it works with Linux right out of the box. I plugged it into my Peppermint Linux system and the kernel immediately recognized the drive and made it available. It was on me to mount the drive, but this was a simple matter and I was able to access the file system and see drive statistics. Obviously it works with Windows so I won’t go into that.

This is a physically small device, slightly less than half the size of a cell phone (iPhone 6s is what I used for comparison). It will easily fit inside the change pocket in my jeans and can tuck just about anywhere. This is a double-edged sword. On one hand it is convenient to have something this small and easy to store, but it is also easy to misplace or even lose. If this stays in your laptop bag or briefcase it should be secure, but if you are in a habit of keeping things in your pockets instead be cautious.

Transfer speeds are good. I have not done benchmarks on this drive but I copied thousands of pictures (average size about 8mb per file, some more and some less) and it was significantly faster than the USB drive I have been using for a while and faster than many of the thumb drives I have been using for backups. I have no complaints.

This is a small and fast drive that just works. It works with Linux which for me is important, and it is small enough to tuck in my camera bag for making backups in the field.
text_fidelity_b: Crucial X6 4TB Portable SSD - Up to 800MB/s - PC and Mac - USB 3.2 USB-C External Solid State Drive - CT4000X6SSD9
